transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time: 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim, Owen Grant, Priya Nair (Hearthside)
Shared: Redwood demo deck (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/hearthside-demo) and sample reranker notebook

[00:00:08] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining um we have about 40 minutes today, we'll do a quick walkthrough of the hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints and then a short console demo. if we run over we can follow up.
[00:00:20] Laura: sounds good, thanks maya. quick context — editorial search is our main pain right now, relevancy drops with long-tail queries. looking to improve click-through and time-on-article.
[00:00:32] Maya: great, super helpful. Samir's gonna walk the technical bits. Samir over to you.
[00:00:36] Samir: yep thanks maya. so high level the pattern we recommend is a two-stage pipeline: first fetch candidates with an approximate vector search (you can use your vector DB), then call our hosted embeddings endpoint to re-embed or use existing embeddings and finally call our reranker endpoint which uses a cross-encoder style scoring. we'll show the endpoints and a live example.
[00:01:05] Owen: small note, currently we precompute embeddings with an in-house model and store them in Pinecone, we also do dot-product similarity — curious how the reranker integrates without re-indexing everything.
[00:01:18] Samir: good question. you don't need to re-index. common approach: keep your existing vector store for candidate retrieval, then send top-K (say 50) candidates to the reranker endpoint along with the query; the reranker uses the text + query pair to score. we also support passing precomputed embedding vectors for faster scoring if you want to skip text roundtrips.
[00:01:41] Priya: what's the payload size limit for the reranker? some of our docs are long (2-3k tokens).
[00:01:48] Samir: currently payloads up to 8,000 tokens are supported on the higher-tier hosted instances, but cost and latency go up with sequence length. for long docs we recommend chunking and passing chunk titles + snippets. we can also demo prefix caching to reduce token counts.
[00:02:10] [00:02:10] Speaker 1: (mumble) -> i think a question on latency tradeoffs.
[00:02:14] Maya: yep latency vs cost is the big one. Samir, can you show the console settings for model choice and batching?
[00:02:20] Samir: sure. share screen — okay on the Redwood Console you pick the model profile for embeddings (we surface open models with verified perf). here I've selected redwood-embed-large-hosted, you can toggle quantization-friendly variants, and set batching parameters like max_batch_ms and max_batch_size.
[00:02:45] Samir: important note: continuous batching reduces per-token cost dramatically but increases median latency slightly. for editorial search where p95 matters, you can set a max latency SLO and we recommend small batches with prefix caching.
[00:03:04] Laura: prefix caching — can you explain that?
[00:03:07] Samir: prefix caching stores KV-cache for repeated prefixes, for chat it's obvious, for rerank pipelines you can cache embedding vectors for canonical metadata fields or frequently repeated query termini. reduces compute on warm hits.
[00:03:25] Owen: are caches shared across tenants in hosted? we need isolation.
[00:03:29] Samir: caches are per-customer in hosted; they're isolated logically. if you move to Dedicated you get physical isolation and control plane separation.
[00:03:40] Priya: on security — SOC2 and KMS. we need to ensure logs and data retention match our retention policy and keys are customer-managed.
[00:03:50] Maya: we have SOC2 Type II and can integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated. for hosted we offer encrypted-at-rest and can discuss bring-your-own-key in enterprise plans. i'll attach the security packet after the call.
[00:03:59] [00:03:59] Laura: ok good. next, can we see an API example for calling embeddings + reranker?
[00:04:05] Samir: yep. example — make a POST to /v1/embeddings with input array, then to /v1/rerank with body: query, candidates (text or ids), top_k. here's a short pseudo-snippet:
[00:04:22] Samir: "POST /v1/rerank {
  \"query\": \"how to tie a scarf\",
  \"candidates\": [{\"id\":1, \"text\":\"...\"}, ...],
  \"top_k\": 5
}"
[00:04:38] Owen: do you support returning explanation tokens or heatscores for debugging?
[00:04:42] Samir: we can return token-level attributions in debug mode. it'll increase latency; we usually recommend sampling during eval runs.
[00:04:51] Maya: sharing a link to the notebook that runs a sample candidate rerank with our hosted endpoints — live result after this call. (link posted in chat)
[00:04:59] [00:04:59] Laura: nice. cost question — if we rerank 50 candidates per query at 1M queries/month what's the rough cost?
[00:05:10] Maya: ballpark depends on model family and token counts; i'll put exact numbers in the pricing sheet but for initial estimate rerank cost per request tends to be higher than a single embedding but for 50 candidates you amortize retrieval cost. we'll calculate a rough monthly estimate and include options for Dedicated reserved capacity which can drastically reduce unit costs.
[00:05:33] Owen: for the bench we'd like p95 under 350ms for rerank on average doc length 512 tokens, is that realistic on hosted?
[00:05:42] Samir: on hosted it depends on chosen model and batch configuration. for smaller cross-encoder models p95 ~200-400ms is plausible; for larger models you'll need Dedicated. we can run a benchmark with your sample queries to confirm.
[00:05:58] Priya: about integrating with our auth — we use SAML SSO and have strict IP allowlist. any considerations?
[00:06:06] Maya: SSO is supported for Redwood Console users; API uses API keys tied to workspace and RBAC. For IP restrictions we can configure customer-level network policies and for Private deployments there are VPC options.
[00:06:20] [00:06:20] Speaker 2: minor static on audio, sorry.
[00:06:24] Samir: practical demo — i'm going to run a live rerank. sending a query "best ways to repurpose longform articles". retrieving 30 candidates from vector store then calling rerank.
[00:06:38] Samir: results — top 3 look like: 1) 'How we turned long articles into short explainers' 2) 'Repurposing long reads for newsletters' 3) 'Summarization workflows for editors' — you can see the score deltas and relevance anchors in the Console.
[00:06:58] Laura: those look promising. can the reranker take signals like recency or click-through as features?
[00:07:05] Samir: yes you can pass metadata features per candidate; the reranker accepts a features field and will integrate them into the final score. we support numeric and categorical features out of the box.
[00:07:18] Owen: do you log training data or keep examples that could be used to fine-tune models? we cannot leak product data.
[00:07:24] Maya: hosted default is not to use customer data to train models. we can provide formal guarantees in the security packet; with Dedicated/Private you control the environment.
[00:07:36] Priya: what's retention on request logs and can we set custom retention?
[00:07:39] Samir: yes retention is configurable per account; default is 30 days, enterprise plans can extend this and we can push logs to your SIEM.
[00:07:48] [00:07:48] Laura: any benchmarks for recall/precision improvements when using reranker vs vanilla nearest neighbor?
[00:07:53] Samir: typical improvements depend on dataset but on editorial corpora we've seen +8-15% MAP and notable uplift in first-click rate. in our deck i linked a case study where CTR improved 12% after reranking.
[00:08:10] Maya: ok quick detour — Console look: under "Optimize" we surface unit cost breakdowns per model, token histograms, and per-route latency. you can pin a model to a route and do canary rollouts to test quality changes.
[00:08:29] Owen: can we automate rollouts tied to evaluation suites? like if quality drops, rollback automatically?
[00:08:34] Samir: yes, Redwood Optimize supports eval sets and quality monitors with automatic rollback rules; you can tie to prompts and success metrics.
[00:08:45] Priya: about dataset upload — we store embeddings in our system or you want them in your vector DB?
[00:08:50] Samir: flexible — many customers keep embeddings in their DB and call rerank; others push to Redwood for managed retrieval. for editorial pipelines customers often prefer their vector DB.
[00:08:58] [00:08:58] Laura: ok security again — can i get the SOC2 report and encryption details?
[00:09:02] Maya: yes i'll attach the SOC2 Type II and the security packet post-call.
[00:09:06] Samir: now a short note on batching — for high qps, we recommend setting max_batch_ms to 20-50ms for low-latency needs or 200-500ms if you want cost efficiency. this is tunable per-route.
[00:09:23] Owen: does Redwood support quantized model variants to save cost?
[00:09:27] Samir: yes, we offer quantization-friendly variants; for rerank we provide int8-like variants that maintain quality for many workloads. recommended after you validate against your eval set.
[00:09:40] [00:09:40] Speaker 1: (laugh) sorry kids in background.
[00:09:44] Laura: question about logs — who has access at Redwood to request metadata?
[00:09:49] Maya: access is limited to the security team and platform engineers for support tickets; we can provide an access log and it's covered in the SLA.
[00:09:58] Samir: demo note — i'm going to show the reranker debug view, i'm turning on token-attribution for one request. you'll see contributing spans and a heat score per candidate.
[00:10:10] Samir: (typing) sending request... result — candidate 7 shows high alignment on the second paragraph; this helps editors tune title/snippet selection.
[00:10:24] Priya: useful. for bench plan, what's needed from our side?
[00:10:29] Samir: we'll need a sample of queries (~5k), representative candidate set per query, and target latency/quality SLOs. Owen agreed earlier to share that.
[00:10:39] Owen: yes i'll export a 5k sample and a small set of candidate docs.
[00:10:43] Maya: i'll include instructions in the bench plan.
[00:10:46] [00:10:46] Laura: are there breakpoints where Dedicated becomes cheaper than hosted?
[00:10:51] Maya: yes generally at sustained high qps and large model usage Dedicated with reserved capacity yields a big discount; we'll run cost modeling for your estimated traffic.
[00:11:03] Samir: one more advanced tip — use feature-weighting in reranker to upweight recency for time-sensitive content. it's a simple scalar per-candidate passed in features.
[00:11:14] Laura: nice. any limitations on features?
[00:11:16] Samir: numeric and low-cardinality categorical features are fine; high-cardinality categories should be hashed or encoded client-side.
[00:11:27] [00:11:27] Maya: quick recap before we wrap — action items: maya to send pricing and security docs; samir to prepare bench plan; owen to send sample queries. we also schedule a technical benchmark next week. does that work for everyone?
[00:11:42] Laura: yes that works.
[00:11:44] Owen: fine with that.
[00:11:46] Priya: yep.
[00:11:48] Maya: perfect. any final questions?
[00:11:51] Laura: just one tiny ask — can we get a short notebook that does the end-to-end candidate->rerank flow with Pinecone?
[00:11:58] Samir: yup i'll attach a Pinecone notebook variant and a generic one.
[00:12:03] Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up with the attachments and next steps.
[00:12:08] [00:12:08] END MARKER: call ended at ~14:52 PDT.
